outcome: Preterm birth (very preterm, moderately preterm, planned preterm)
cohort: Breast cancer survivors who gave birth to singletons in Sweden between 1973 and 2017 (n=926), matched to a comparator cohort of women without breast cancer (n=92,490)
finding: Women who conceived within 2 years of a breast cancer diagnosis had higher risks of preterm birth, induced delivery, and cesarean section, while those conceiving after 2 years showed no increased risks compared to women without breast cancer.
mod_finding: Women who conceived within 1 year after breast cancer diagnosis had a higher risk of cesarean section (RR; 1.7, 1.0-2.7) compared to those without a breast cancer diagnosis.
birth_weight: Low birthweight was analyzed as an outcome.
